mainTopic: Who disqualifies a woman from תרומה and כהונה: the ארוס, the חרש, the nine-year-old, and the פסוק source for disqualification by an unfit man
overview: The גמרא finishes explaining the משנה's list of men who disqualify a woman from eating תרומה but do not let her eat it. A ארוס and a חרש both disqualify a כהן's daughter. Neither lets a בת ישראל eat, because of עולא's decree and because a חרש cannot make a תורה-level acquisition. For the nine-year-old, אביי says he is a יבם whose ביאה the חכמים treated like an adult's מאמר. רבא rejects this because it would make the משנה's ספק case pointless. רבא instead explains that the boy belongs to the unfit groups whose relations disqualify a woman, and he proves it from a ברייתא. The גמרא then studies that ברייתא, including the views of רבי יוסי and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל. Finally, רב finds the source in the פסוק ״ובת כהן כי תהיה לאיש זר״. After a back-and-forth about which פסוק teaches the ban on a married כהן's daughter eating תרומה, the גמרא concludes that the ban comes from ״וכל זר לא יאכל קדש״.

steps.title: Finishing the case of the betrothed man
steps.stepSummary: A ארוס disqualifies a כהן's daughter from תרומה because his betrothal truly acquires her. But a כהן who is only betrothed to a בת ישראל does not let her eat, because of עולא's rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since he acquired her through betrothal (he disqualifies her). And if she is an Israelite woman betrothed to a כהן, he does not let her eat תרומה, because of עולא's reason.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing its explanation of the ארוס from the משנה. It shows why he disqualifies but does not let her eat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For disqualifying, real קידושין is enough: once she is betrothed to an Israelite, a כהן's daughter loses her right to her father's תרומה. For letting her eat, the תורה alone would allow it, but עולא taught that the חכמים forbade a betrothed woman to eat תרומה. So the ארוס ends up in the 'disqualifies but does not let her eat' group.

keyTerms.meaning: He acquired her (as a wife)
'Becoming his', meaning קידושין (betrothal)
Disqualifies her from eating תרומה
Lets her eat תרומה

phrases.english: since he acquired her through betrothal.
phrases.notes: This finishes a sentence that started earlier: a כהן's daughter betrothed to an Israelite is disqualified.

phrases.english: And if she is an Israelite woman betrothed to a priest,
he does not let her eat, because of Ulla.
phrases.notes: עולא taught that the חכמים forbade a betrothed woman to eat תרומה, even though the תורה would allow it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the explanation of the ארוס from before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A ארוס disqualifies (real קידושין) but does not let her eat (rabbinic decree of עולא).

steps.title: Why a deaf-mute disqualifies but does not let her eat
steps.stepSummary: A חרש's marriage works only by rabbinic decree. That is enough to disqualify a כהן's daughter, but not enough to give a בת ישראל the תורה status of 'קנין כספו'.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the deaf-mute: if she is a כהן's daughter married to an Israelite deaf-mute, he disqualifies her, because he acquired her through a rabbinic decree. And if she is an Israelite woman married to a deaf-mute כהן, he does not let her eat. The תורה says 'the purchase of his money', and this man is not able to acquire.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next item in the משנה, the חרש, and explains both halves of his law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים made a חרש's marriage valid, so a כהן's daughter married to him counts as married and loses her father's תרומה. But letting her eat requires the תורה condition of 'קנין כספו', a real acquisition by תורה law. A חרש cannot make a תורה-level acquisition, so his wife cannot eat.

keyTerms.meaning: A deaf-mute, who is not legally competent by תורה law
A decree of the חכמים
'The purchase of his money': the פסוק that lets a כהן's household eat תרומה
Someone legally able to acquire

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a key pattern in the סוגיא: a rabbinic marriage is enough to disqualify, but letting a woman eat needs a תורה-level acquisition.

phrases.english: And the deaf-mute.

phrases.aramaic: אִי בַּת כֹּהֵן לְיִשְׂרָאֵל הִיא — פָּסֵיל לַהּ,
phrases.english: If she is a priest's daughter married to an Israelite, he disqualifies her,
since he acquired her through a decree of the Rabbis.

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי בַּת יִשְׂרָאֵל לְכֹהֵן הִיא — לָא מַאֲכֵיל,
phrases.english: And if she is an Israelite woman married to a priest, he does not let her eat,
'the purchase of his money', says the Merciful One,
and this one is not capable of acquiring.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next case in the משנה's list, using the same two-sided format.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A חרש's rabbinic marriage disqualifies a כהן's daughter but cannot let a בת ישראל eat, since he is not a בר קנין by תורה law.

steps.title: First guess about the nine-year-old in the משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes 'a nine-year-old' from the משנה and first assumes it means a widow waiting for a nine-year-old יבם.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And a nine-year-old' and so on. We assume at first that it means a woman waiting for a יבם who is nine years and one day old.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא quotes the next case and states a first assumption, which it will attack in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'קא סלקא דעתין' tell us this is only a first assumption. The case pictured is a שומרת יבם whose יבם is nine years and a day old and has not yet done anything with her.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It enters our mind': our first assumption
A widow waiting for her יבם (brother-in-law) to do יבום

phrases.english: And a nine-year-old, etc.
It enters our mind

phrases.aramaic: בְּשׁוֹמֶרֶת יָבָם לְבֶן תֵּשַׁע וְיוֹם אֶחָד.
phrases.english: that it refers to a woman waiting for a nine-year-and-one-day-old yavam.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the discussion of the next item in the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What case does the משנה's 'nine-year-old' refer to?

steps.title: Why would age nine matter at all?
steps.stepSummary: If the case is a waiting widow, age nine makes no difference. Even a younger יבם disqualifies her, and even an adult יבם does not let her eat.
steps.simpleTranslation: For what purpose? If for disqualifying, a younger boy also disqualifies. If for letting her eat, an adult also does not let her eat!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the first assumption: under that reading, mentioning 'nine years and a day' teaches nothing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A שומרת יבם is tied to her יבם whatever his age, so even a younger boy keeps her from going back to eat her father's תרומה. And no יבם, even an adult, lets her eat before יבום. So the age detail seems pointless.

keyTerms.meaning: For what purpose? What does it come to teach?
A minor, younger than nine years and a day here
An adult

phrases.english: For what?

phrases.aramaic: אִי לְמִיפְסַל — קָטָן נָמֵי מִיפְסָל פָּסֵיל,
phrases.english: If to disqualify, a younger one also disqualifies,

phrases.aramaic: אִי לְאוֹכוֹלֵי — גָּדוֹל נָמֵי לֹא מַאֲכִיל!
phrases.english: if to let her eat, an adult also does not let her eat!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the first assumption from step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: The assumption that the משנה speaks of a waiting widow with a nine-year-old יבם.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Under that reading the age adds nothing on either side: a younger יבם also disqualifies, and an older one also does not let her eat.

steps.title: אביי: the nine-year-old already had relations with her
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains that the משנה means a nine-year-old יבם who already had relations with his יבמה, which acquires her by תורה law.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: Here we are dealing with a nine-year-and-one-day-old יבם who had relations with his יבמה, since by תורה law she is acquired by him.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the challenge by changing the case: the boy has already done יבום with her.
steps.deeperAnalysis: At nine years and a day, a boy's relations count by תורה law, so his ביאה really acquires the יבמה. That is why the age matters: below this age his act would mean nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Here we are dealing with...': narrowing the case
Who had relations with his יבמה
By תורה law

phrases.english: Abaye said:

phrases.aramaic: הָכָא בְּיָבָם בֶּן תֵּשַׁע שָׁנִים וְיוֹם אֶחָד
phrases.english: Here, with a yavam nine years and one day old
who had relations with his yevama, we are dealing.
for by Torah law she is acquired by him,

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: הָכָא בְּיָבָם בֶּן תֵּשַׁע שָׁנִים וְיוֹם אֶחָד הַבָּא עַל יְבִמְתּוֹ עָסְקִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 4 by redefining the case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה speaks of a waiting widow whose nine-year-old יבם did nothing yet.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה speaks of a nine-year-old יבם who already had relations with her, acquiring her by תורה law.

steps.title: The Rabbis treated his relations like an adult's מאמר
steps.stepSummary: We might think his תורה-level acquisition lets her eat. The משנה teaches that the חכמים gave a nine-year-old's ביאה the status of an adult's מאמר, so she may not eat.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have thought: since by תורה law she is acquired by him, and his relations count as relations, let him allow her to eat. So the משנה teaches us that the חכמים made the relations of a nine-year-and-one-day-old boy like a מאמר done by an adult.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי explains why the משנה needed to teach this case: to block the thought that the boy's real acquisition lets her eat תרומה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By תורה law his ביאה is a full acquisition, so we would expect her to eat. But the חכמים lowered it to the level of an adult's מאמר, which is only a rabbinic betrothal of a יבמה. A מאמר does not let her eat, so this does not either. Like any acquisition, though, it still disqualifies.

keyTerms.meaning: 'You might have thought': introduces the mistaken idea
'It teaches us': the real point
Relations, the act that completes יבום
A rabbinic betrothal of a יבמה with money or a document

steps.whatToRemember: According to אביי (whose reading רבא rejects in Steps 7–8), a nine-year-old יבם who had relations with his יבמה acquires her by תורה law, but the חכמים treated his act like an adult's מאמר. So he disqualifies her but does not let her eat תרומה.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the nine-year-old's ביאה is meaningless. By תורה law it really acquires her. The חכמים only limited its effect, so it counts like a מאמר and does not let her eat.

phrases.english: It might enter your mind to say:
since by Torah law she is acquired by him
and his relations count as relations, say he lets her eat;
so it teaches us

phrases.aramaic: עָשׂוּ בִּיאַת בֶּן תֵּשַׁע שָׁנִים וְיוֹם אֶחָד
phrases.english: they made the relations of a nine-year-and-one-day-old
like a ma'amar by an adult.

steps.triggerLanguage: סָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ אָמֵינָא: הוֹאִיל וּמִדְּאוֹרָיְיתָא קַנְיָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes אביי's answer by explaining what the משנה comes to teach in his case.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: In אביי's explanation, the חכמים treated a nine-year-old's ביאה like an adult's מאמר, so it disqualifies but does not let the יבמה eat תרומה.

steps.title: רבא asks: why mention a doubtful nine-year-old?
steps.stepSummary: רבא argues that אביי's reading makes the סיפא of the משנה about a ספק pointless.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to אביי: If so, look at the end of the משנה, which talks about a boy who may or may not be nine years and one day old. If a boy who is definitely nine does not let her eat, do we even need to be told that a doubtful one does not?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא attacks אביי's explanation from Step 5. If he is right, the next line of the משנה would be teaching something obvious.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to אביי, the big new idea was that even a definite nine-year-old's ביאה does not let her eat תרומה. If that is true, a boy who might not even be nine certainly cannot let her eat. So the משנה's line about the ספק would add nothing, and a משנה does not waste words.

keyTerms.meaning: The latter (end) clause of a משנה or ברייתא
A doubt; a case where we are unsure of the facts
Certain, definite
Enables (her) to eat תרומה
Is it necessary (to say)? This signals that the point is obvious

phrases.english: Rava said to him: If so,
phrases.notes: "Him" is אביי, whose explanation we just saw.

phrases.english: the latter clause, which teaches:

phrases.aramaic: סָפֵק בֶּן תֵּשַׁע שָׁנִים וְיוֹם אֶחָד
phrases.english: a doubt whether he is nine years and one day old
or a doubt whether he is not —

phrases.aramaic: הַשְׁתָּא וַדַּאי בֶּן תֵּשַׁע לֹא מַאֲכִיל,
phrases.english: now, if one who is definitely nine does not enable her to eat,
is it necessary to say so about a doubtful one?!

steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's explanation that the משנה means a nine-year-old יבם who had relations with his יבמה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If a definite nine-year-old cannot let her eat, a doubtful one obviously cannot either. That would make the סיפא about a ספק unnecessary.

steps.title: רבא: the משנה means a nine-year-old from the unfit groups
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that the משנה refers to a nine-year-old from the groups of פסולים whose relations disqualify a woman.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא said: the משנה is talking about a boy of nine years and one day who belongs to those unfit groups that disqualify a woman through their relations.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא drops אביי's reading and gives his own explanation of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה is no longer about a יבם. It is about a nine-year-old who is himself פסול, such as a ממזר. His ביאה at nine already makes a woman unfit for a כהן. So the ספק clause now teaches something new: even a boy who might be nine disqualifies her, out of doubt.

keyTerms.meaning: Men who are unfit (to marry into the Jewish people or into כהונה)
They disqualify (a woman from marrying a כהן or eating תרומה)
Marital relations

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix this up with אביי's case. רבא is no longer talking about a יבם at all. He is talking about a boy whose relations make a woman פסולה because he himself belongs to a disqualified group.

phrases.english: Rather, Rava said:
about a boy nine years and one day old
who is one of those unfit people, it is teaching,
phrases.notes: "Those unfit people" are the groups listed in the ברייתא that comes right next.

phrases.english: who disqualify a woman through their relations.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces אביי's reading, which Step 7 knocked down.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case of the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה is about a nine-year-old יבם, which makes the ספק clause redundant.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה is about a nine-year-old פסול whose ביאה disqualifies her. The ספק clause adds that even a doubtful age disqualifies.

steps.title: A ברייתא lists the unfit nine-year-olds
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא supports רבא: a nine-year-old from the unfit groups who has relations with a woman disqualifies her.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: a boy of nine years and one day who is an Ammonite or Moabite convert, an Egyptian or Edomite, a כותי, a נתין, a חלל or a ממזר, who had relations with the daughter of a כהן, a לוי or a ישראל, has disqualified her.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא brings a ברייתא to show that his kind of case really exists in the sources.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says clearly that a nine-year-old from these groups makes a woman פסולה through his ביאה. This is exactly the case רבא says the משנה is talking about. The ruling covers every woman, whether her father is a כהן, a לוי or a ישראל.

keyTerms.meaning: A convert
A descendant of the Gibeonites, who may not marry into the Jewish people
A son of a כהן born from a forbidden union; he lost his כהונה status
A child born from a forbidden union such as incest or adultery
A Samaritan

phrases.english: And as it was taught in a ברייתא:
A boy nine years and one day old
who is an Ammonite or Moabite convert,
an Egyptian or an Edomite, a Samaritan,
a Gibeonite, a חלל or a ממזר
who had relations with a כהן's daughter, a Levite's daughter or a Yisrael's daughter —
they have disqualified her.
phrases.notes: He means she can no longer marry a כהן, and a כהן's daughter also loses her right to eat תרומה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבא's new reading from Step 8.
steps.raayaObject: רבא's claim that a nine-year-old פסול disqualifies a woman through his ביאה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא listing the unfit groups whose nine-year-olds disqualify a woman.

steps.title: The next משנה seems to deal with unfit men separately
steps.stepSummary: The next משנה treats unfit men as its own case, which suggests the earlier משנה was not about unfit men.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the later משנה teaches: 'If they are not fit to enter into Israel, they disqualify her.' This implies that the earlier clause is not dealing with unfit men!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבא's reading from the wording of the next משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the later משנה has to introduce unfit men as a new case, then the earlier משנה must have been about men who are fit. That goes against רבא, who said the earlier משנה already deals with פסולים.

keyTerms.meaning: The first (opening) clause
It follows by implication that
We are dealing with

phrases.english: But since the latter clause teaches:
phrases.notes: The "latter clause" here is the next משנה (69a).

phrases.english: if they are not fit to enter into Israel
— these disqualify her,
it follows that in the first clause
we are not dealing with unfit men!

steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's claim that the earlier משנה deals with nine-year-old פסולים.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A later clause about unfit men implies the earlier clause was about men who are fit.

steps.title: Two different kinds of unfit men
steps.stepSummary: The first clause deals with פסולי קהל and the latter with פסולי כהונה, so both clauses are needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: The first clause is about men unfit to marry into the Jewish people. The latter clause is about men unfit only for כהונה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge and keeps רבא's reading.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two kinds of פסולים. Some cannot marry into the Jewish community at all, and others are unfit only for the כהונה. Each clause deals with a different kind, so the later clause does not prove that the earlier one is about fit men.

keyTerms.meaning: Men unfit to marry into the Jewish community
Men unfit only for the priesthood

steps.whatToRemember: רבא's reading stands. The משנה's nine-year-old is a פסול whose ביאה disqualifies a woman. The two clauses cover two different kinds of פסולים.

phrases.english: The first clause is about those unfit for the community,
the latter clause is about those unfit for the priesthood.

steps.triggerLanguage: רֵישָׁא פְּסוּלֵי קָהָל, סֵיפָא פְּסוּלֵי כְהוּנָּה
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases of the two clauses
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The latter clause introduces unfit men, so the first clause must be about fit men.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both clauses deal with unfit men of different kinds: קהל in the first, כהונה in the latter.

steps.title: The ברייתא quoted again for its own discussion
steps.stepSummary: With 'גופא', the גמרא quotes the ברייתא again so it can now study it directly.
steps.simpleTranslation: The matter itself: a boy of nine years and one day who is an Ammonite or Moabite convert, an Egyptian or Edomite, a כותי, a נתין, a חלל or a ממזר, who had relations with the daughter of a כהן, a לוי or a ישראל, has disqualified her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a new discussion. It repeats the ברייתא it used as proof so it can now analyze the ברייתא itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before, the ברייתא was only a support for רבא. Now the word גופא shows the ברייתא becomes the topic of its own discussion. The questions about it come next.

keyTerms.meaning: "The matter itself". It opens a direct discussion of a source quoted earlier

phrases.english: The matter itself:
A boy nine years and one day old
who is an Ammonite or Moabite convert,
an Egyptian or an Edomite, a Samaritan,
a Gibeonite, a חלל or a ממזר
who had relations with a כהן's daughter, a Levite's daughter or a Yisrael's daughter —
they have disqualified her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Repeats the ברייתא from Step 9 so the גמרא can now discuss it on its own.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A nine-year-old from these unfit groups disqualifies any woman he has relations with from marrying a כהן.

steps.title: Two more opinions in the ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues with two more views. רבי יוסי says that a man disqualifies a woman if his children are unfit. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says that a man disqualifies a woman if you may not marry his daughter.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי says: anyone whose children are unfit disqualifies her, and anyone whose children are not unfit does not disqualify her. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says: anyone whose daughter you may marry, you may marry his widow. Anyone whose daughter you may not marry, you may not marry his widow.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא keeps quoting the ברייתא it began in the last step. Here it gives two more opinions on which men disqualify a woman through relations.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי makes the test about the man's children: if his offspring are unfit, he disqualifies the woman. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל makes it about his daughter: if she may not be married, his widow (or partner) also becomes unfit for a כהן. Both views give a general rule for deciding which men disqualify.

keyTerms.meaning: His offspring, his children
Disqualifies (makes the woman unfit to marry a כהן)
Marries
His widow

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei says:
Anyone whose offspring is unfit disqualifies her,
phrases.notes: He means: if this man's children could not marry into the Jewish people, then his relations with a woman make her unfit for a כהן.

phrases.aramaic: כֹּל שֶׁאֵין זַרְעוֹ פָּסוּל — אֵינוֹ פּוֹסֵל.
phrases.english: anyone whose offspring is not unfit does not disqualify her.
Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:
Anyone whose daughter you may marry,
you may marry his widow,
and anyone whose daughter you may not marry,
you may not marry his widow.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר: כֹּל שֶׁזַּרְעוֹ פָּסוּל — פּוֹסֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא that the גמרא started quoting with גופא in step 12.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוסי: a man whose offspring are unfit disqualifies a woman through relations. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל: a man whose daughter may not be married disqualifies his widow from marrying a כהן.

steps.title: Asking for the source of the rule
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where we learn that relations with an unfit man disqualify a woman.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where are these things learned?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the source in the תורה for the rule it has been discussing. This question sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Up to now the discussion has been about who disqualifies a woman. Now the גמרא wants the פסוק that shows relations with an unfit man disqualify her at all.

keyTerms.meaning: From where are these things learned? (a request for the source)

phrases.english: From where are these matters derived?
phrases.notes: He means the rule that relations with an unfit man make a woman unfit for a כהן and for eating תרומה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Now that the ברייתא has been quoted in full, the גמרא asks for the פסוק behind its basic rule.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The פסוק that teaches that relations with an unfit man disqualify a woman.

steps.title: רב finds the source in ״איש זר״
steps.stepSummary: רב teaches that the source is the פסוק ״ובת כהן כי תהיה לאיש זר״. A man who is unfit for her counts as a זר, an outsider, and his relations disqualify her.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רב: the פסוק says, 'And if a כהן's daughter is with a stranger.' Once she had relations with a man who is unfit for her, he disqualified her.
steps.whatsHappening: רב answers the question by pointing to a פסוק about a כהן's daughter and an ״איש זר״.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב reads ״איש זר″ as a man who is foreign to her, meaning one she is not allowed to be with. So the פסוק is teaching that relations with such a man disqualify her.

keyTerms.meaning: The פסוק says
A stranger, an outsider (here: a man unfit for her)
She had relations

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:
The verse states:
"And if a priest's daughter be married to a common man,"
since she had relations with one who is unfit for her,
he disqualified her.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב, אָמַר קְרָא
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The source is ״ובת כהן כי תהיה לאיש זר״. An ״איש זר″ means a man unfit for her, and relations with him disqualify her.

steps.title: That פסוק is needed for a different law
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that ״איש זר״ is needed to teach that a כהן's daughter married to a non-כהן may not eat תרומה. If so, it cannot also be the source for רב's rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: But this פסוק is needed for what the תורה says: a כהן's daughter who marries a non-כהן may not eat תרומה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב. It says his פסוק is already being used for another law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The simple meaning of ״זר״ is a non-כהן, even one she is allowed to marry. The פסוק then teaches that marrying such a man stops her from eating תרומה. If the words are needed for that, they are not free to teach רב's rule.

keyTerms.meaning: It is needed for (a different teaching)
The Merciful One (the תורה)
She marries
She may not eat (תרומה)

phrases.english: That verse is needed
for what the Merciful One says:
a priest's daughter who marries a non-priest
may not eat!
phrases.notes: She may not eat תרומה, the holy food that a כהן's family eats.

steps.kashyaTarget: רב's reading of ״איש זר״ as the source for disqualification through an unfit man.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק is already needed for the law that a כהן's daughter married to a non-כהן may not eat תרומה, so it cannot also teach רב's rule.

steps.title: The תרומה law comes from a later פסוק
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the תרומה law is learned from ״ושבה אל בית אביה... תאכל״. If she eats only when she returns to her father's house, then while she was married she could not eat. So ״איש זר״ is free to teach רב's rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: That law comes from 'And she returns to her father's house as in her youth, she may eat of her father's bread.' Since the תורה says 'she returns to her father's house... she may eat,' we can infer that at first, while she was married, she could not eat.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב. It shows that the other law has its own source, so רב's פסוק is not needed for it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The next פסוק says she may eat again once she returns to her father's house as a widow or divorcee. That means she was not allowed to eat while she was married to the non-כהן. Since that law is learned from there, ״איש זר״ is free to teach that an unfit man disqualifies her.

keyTerms.meaning: It is learned (literally, it comes out)
And she returns to her father's house
By implication, we can infer
At first, originally

phrases.aramaic: הָהִיא, מִ״וְּשָׁבָה אֶל בֵּית אָבִיהָ כִּנְעוּרֶיהָ
phrases.english: That law is derived from "and is returned to her father's house, as in her youth,
she may eat of her father's bread."
From the fact that the Merciful One says:
"And is returned to her father's house... she may eat,"
it may be inferred that at first she could not eat.
phrases.notes: At first means while she was still married to the non-כהן.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָהִיא, מִ״וְּשָׁבָה אֶל בֵּית אָבִיהָ כִּנְעוּרֶיהָ מִלֶּחֶם אָבִיהָ תֹּאכֵל״ נָפְקָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 16 and keeps רב's source in place.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Moving the competing law to a different פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: ״איש זר״ is needed to forbid תרומה to a כהן's daughter married to a non-כהן.
steps.terutzMaskana: That law comes from ״ושבה אל בית אביה... תאכל״, so ״איש זר״ is free to teach that an unfit man disqualifies her.

steps.title: The verse ״ושבה אל בית אביה״ only gives a weaker command
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the answer of step 17. From ״ושבה אל בית אביה״ alone we would only have a לאו הבא מכלל עשה, which counts as an עשה. So the תורה wrote ״איש זר״ to make it a real לאו.
steps.simpleTranslation: If we only had that verse, I would have said that a prohibition that comes out of a positive command counts as a positive command. So the תורה wrote this verse to make it a real prohibition.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on step 17's answer. It says ״איש זר״ is still needed for the תרומה law after all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ״ושבה אל בית אביה... תאכל״ is worded as a positive statement: she eats when she returns. The ban on eating while married is only implied, and an implied ban like that has only the strength of an עשה. To give it the force of a real לאו, the תורה needed ״איש זר״, so it is not free for רב's rule.

keyTerms.meaning: I would have said; the mistaken idea we would have had
A prohibition that we only learn by implication from a positive command
A positive command; weaker than a לאו in punishment
A direct prohibition, a 'do not'
The Merciful One; the תורה

steps.confusionAlert: The question is not whether she may eat תרומה. Everyone agrees she may not. The question is how strong the prohibition is: a weaker עשה or a full לאו.

phrases.english: If it were only from that verse, I would have said:
phrases.notes: "That verse" is ״ושבה אל בית אביה... תאכל״ from step 17.

phrases.english: a prohibition that comes from a positive command counts as a positive command,
so the Merciful One wrote this verse to make it a real prohibition.
phrases.notes: "This verse" is ״ובת כהן כי תהיה לאיש זר״.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects step 17's answer and brings back step 16's objection.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The claim that ״ושבה אל בית אביה״ fully covers the תרומה law, leaving ״איש זר״ free.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: That verse gives only a לאו הבא מכלל עשה, which counts as an עשה. ״איש זר״ is still needed to make a full לאו.

steps.title: The real prohibition comes from ״וכל זר לא יאכל קדש״
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the full לאו against her eating תרומה comes from the פסוק ״וכל זר לא יאכל קדש״. So ״איש זר״ is free again to teach רב's rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: The prohibition comes from the verse ״And no outsider may eat the sacred food.״
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the pushback from step 18. It names a different פסוק as the source of the real לאו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ״וכל זר לא יאכל קדש״ is worded as a direct 'do not'. That makes it a full לאו, and it covers the woman married to a זר. Since the לאו already has a source, ״איש זר״ is not needed for it and stays free for רב's rule.

keyTerms.meaning: An outsider; here, someone who is not part of a כהן's household
Sacred food; here, תרומה
It comes out from; it is learned from

steps.whatToRemember: There are three פסוקים in play. ״ושבה אל בית אביה״ gives the implied rule. ״וכל זר לא יאכל קדש״ gives the full לאו. That leaves ״איש זר״ free to teach רב's rule: an unfit man's relations disqualify the woman.

phrases.aramaic: [לָאו] מִ״וְכָל זָר לֹא יֹאכַל קֹדֶשׁ״ נָפְקָא.
phrases.english: The prohibition is learned from "And no outsider may eat the sacred food."
phrases.notes: ויקרא 22:10. The word in square brackets is added in the corrected wording.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָאו מִוְכָל זָר לֹא יֹאכַל קֹדֶשׁ נָפְקָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 18's pushback and brings back step 17's conclusion that ״איש זר״ is free.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Points to a different פסוק as the source of the full לאו.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: ״איש זר״ is needed to turn the implied rule into a full לאו.
steps.terutzMaskana: The full לאו comes from ״וכל זר לא יאכל קדש״, so ״איש זר״ is free to teach רב's rule.
